title: Yearbook and Detention
premise: Xanthe Dravenmoor, a nonbinary coder at Hollowell Academy, runs an anonymous gossip account that has accidentally exposed the wrong people — the school's secret Honor Society, which has quietly ruled the campus for generations. When the legendary ghost of founder Elias Hollowell begins leaving them notes in ink that shouldn't exist, Xanthe discovers the 'ghost' is a dying student kept alive by the Society's stolen power, and that their own account made them the only outsider who can break it. With the help of the misfit yearbook staff they've secretly loved all year, Xanthe must choose between the safe anonymity they hide behind and going on record — and when the Society's corruption finally consumes the ghost's last hours, Xanthe publishes everything, dismantles the Society, and claims their real name for the first time.
about_author: Ada Montrose is the pen name of a former school newspaper editor who grew up in a crumbling New England boarding town and never quite left it. They write stories about kids who find their people in the unglamorous corners of institutions.

chapters.title: The Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. After posting a rumor about the Honor Society's secret midnight meetings, Xanthe finds a note in their locker signed 'E. Hollowell, 1897,' written in ink that shifts color and won't smudge. Terrified but intrigued, they don't tell anyone. The beat is unease — the first crack in Xanthe's carefully managed anonymity.

chapters.title: Detention with the Dead
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Framed for vandalism they didn't commit, Xanthe lands in Saturday detention with the yearbook staff: sharp-tongued Priya, anxious Theo, and quiet Marisol, who flinches at the ghost's name. A second note appears, addressed to Xanthe's real name — the one almost no one knows. The beat is reluctant connection.

chapters.title: What the Yearbook Knows
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Digging through fifty years of yearbooks for the ghost's face, Priya notices the same five students' descendants appear in every 'Honor Society' photo — including Head Prefect Cassius Vane. She and Xanthe compare notes, and an alliance forms. The beat is the thrill of shared conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Terms
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The notes lead Xanthe to the sealed east wing, where they meet the 'ghost': Wren, a student the Society has kept half-alive for decades to anchor its power. Wren offers Xanthe the truth — and a deadline: the anchoring fails at commencement. The beat is horror and responsibility.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, who catalogues everyone at school in the yearbook database, realizes the Society has been doing the same with students — ranking, sorting, owning them. Xanthe's file is flagged 'anomaly.' The staff realizes Xanthe is in danger. The beat is protective anger; found family solidifies.

chapters.title: Cassius Offers a Deal
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Cassius corners Xanthe with an offer: join the Society, keep the account, gain real power — or be erased the way Wren was. He reveals he knows who Xanthe is behind the account. Xanthe stalls, but the temptation of belonging on the winning side is real. The beat is corruption's seduction.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine (It Is Not)
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol, Wren's grand-niece, confesses her family's complicity and gives the group Wren's hidden ledger. The Society retaliates: the yearbook room is ransacked, Theo is suspended, and Xanthe's anonymous account is hijacked to post lies. The beat is the cost of defiance — and resolve hardening anyway.

chapters.title: Commencement Eve
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The staff plans to expose the Society during commencement using the ledger, the hijacked account's trace, and Wren's fading testimony. Xanthe and Wren share a quiet, aching conversation about names, duty, and what it costs to be known. The beat is tender dread before the storm.

chapters.title: The Unmasking
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At commencement, Cassius triggers the anchoring ritual early to save himself, and Wren begins to unravel before the whole school. Xanthe takes the stage, publishes the ledger live, and speaks their real name aloud as the Society's power collapses. The beat is the climax — courage over safety, love over duty.

chapters.title: Signed, Xanthe Dravenmoor
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Weeks later: the Society is dissolved, Wren is finally at rest, and the yearbook staff — now unmistakably family — prints a memorial page no administrator can remove. Xanthe signs their final post with their real name and keeps writing, but honestly now. The beat is grief braided with hope and belonging.
